The Anniversary of a Death

For the anniversary of losing someone, and the days leading up to it. It decides in advance how the day will go, tells one person the date, makes room for something that was theirs, and plans a landing for the morning after.

Anniversaries · Grief · Loss · Self-Compassion · 9 items · whenever you need it

The checklist

  • Decide in advance how you want the day to go — a day you planned is easier than one that arrives.
  • Tell one person what the date is — being quietly held in mind costs them nothing.
  • Take the day off if you can, or the afternoon — grief keeps its own calendar and this is on it.
  • Do one thing that was theirs — a recipe, a walk, a record they wore out.
  • Let the day be smaller or bigger than you feared — the run-up is often worse than the date itself.
  • Write them a few lines you will not send — saying it somewhere is different from saying nothing.
  • Keep 988 in your phone for the hard hours — call or text, any time, free across the United States.
  • Eat something and drink water even if nothing appeals — a grieving body still has to be carried.
  • Plan something ordinary for the next morning — the day after an anniversary needs a landing.

Use this checklist Free account: tick items off and keep each day's record.

How to use it

Run through it whenever you need it, honestly and without scoring yourself. A checklist is a way of noticing, not a test: an item you cannot tick is information about the day, not a verdict on you. Over a few weeks the pattern of what gets ticked and what does not says more than any single pass.

With a free Theraglee account the checklist remembers each pass, so you can look back. Without one, you can still read it here and keep your own copy.
